title: Windows Programming with the Win32 API
tagline: Native Windows applications, from the message loop up
description: A full course on the Windows API in C++: handles, errors and Unicode strings, windows and the message loop, painting, input, menus and resources, controls and dialogs, high DPI, Direct2D and DirectWrite, files, the registry, processes and threads, the clipboard and the shell, and packaging, finishing with a text editor and a file finder. It assumes the first milestones of the C++ course. You build the programs in Visual Studio; the practice on the site checks the logic inside them.

milestones.title: Windows and Messages
milestones.blurb: Handles and errors, UTF-16 strings, window classes and the message loop, how messages work, and painting with GDI.

lessons.title: Handles, Errors and the Documentation
lessons.summary: The Win32 API is thousands of C functions with their own conventions. This lesson explains handles, the Windows type names, how functions report errors through return values and GetLastError, turning error codes into messages, and how to read the documentation.

lessons.title: Strings on Windows
lessons.summary: Windows uses UTF-16 internally, while files and the web mostly use UTF-8. This lesson explains the W and A versions of functions, wchar_t and L"" literals, surrogate pairs, converting between UTF-8 and UTF-16, and the UTF-8 code page option.

lessons.title: Windows, Classes and the Message Loop
lessons.summary: The smallest real Windows program - registering a window class, creating a window, running the message loop, and writing the window procedure that handles messages. This lesson builds it line by line and explains each step.

lessons.title: Messages in Depth
lessons.summary: How messages really flow - posted versus sent messages, the order of messages when a window is created and destroyed, how WPARAM and LPARAM pack several values, storing per-window data, and custom messages of your own.

lessons.title: Painting with GDI
lessons.summary: Windows asks a window to paint itself with WM_PAINT. This lesson handles it with BeginPaint and EndPaint, draws lines, shapes and text with GDI, manages pens, brushes and fonts without leaking them, and invalidates just the part of the window that changed.

projects.title: A model of the message queue

milestones.title: Input, Menus and Controls
milestones.blurb: The keyboard, the mouse, timers and the clock, menus, accelerators and resources, and the standard controls.

lessons.title: Keyboard Input
lessons.summary: Keys arrive as WM_KEYDOWN and WM_KEYUP with virtual-key codes, text arrives as WM_CHAR after TranslateMessage. This lesson explains the difference, the information packed into lParam, auto-repeat, modifier keys, system keys and keyboard focus.

lessons.title: Mouse Input and Capture
lessons.summary: Handling clicks, double-clicks, movement and the wheel, the modifier flags that come with them, capturing the mouse during a drag, knowing when the mouse leaves, setting the cursor, and hit-testing your own shapes.

lessons.title: Timers and the Clock
lessons.summary: Doing things later or repeatedly with SetTimer and WM_TIMER, why timers are not precise, measuring time with QueryPerformanceCounter, the system clock and time zones, and running animation without freezing the interface.

lessons.title: Menus, Accelerators and Resources
lessons.summary: Adding a menu bar and context menus, handling WM_COMMAND, enabling and checking items as the program's state changes, keyboard shortcuts with accelerator tables, and the resource file that holds menus, icons, strings and version information.

lessons.title: Standard Controls
lessons.summary: Buttons, check boxes, edit boxes, list boxes and combo boxes are child windows of classes Windows provides. This lesson creates them, talks to them with messages, handles their notifications, gives them the right font, and moves the keyboard focus between them with Tab.

milestones.title: Dialogs and Modern Interfaces
milestones.blurb: Dialog boxes, the common dialogs, layout when a window is resized, high-DPI screens, and the common controls.

lessons.title: Dialog Boxes
lessons.summary: Dialogs are windows built from a template, with keyboard navigation and default buttons for free. This lesson creates modal and modeless dialogs, writes the dialog procedure, moves data in and out of the controls, validates input, and returns a result.

lessons.title: Common Dialogs
lessons.summary: Windows provides the Open, Save, folder, colour and font dialogs every program needs. This lesson uses the modern IFileOpenDialog and IFileSaveDialog through COM, with file type filters, default extensions and folders, and the older colour and font dialogs.

lessons.title: Layout and Resizing
lessons.summary: Win32 has no layout engine - when a window is resized, you move its controls. This lesson lays controls out in WM_SIZE with anchors, sets a minimum size with WM_GETMINMAXINFO, moves many controls at once without flicker, and builds a splitter.

lessons.title: High-DPI Screens
lessons.summary: Laptops and 4K monitors run at 150 % or 200 % scaling, and a program that ignores it is either tiny or blurry. This lesson declares per-monitor DPI awareness, scales sizes and fonts with the DPI, handles moving between monitors with WM_DPICHANGED, and picks the right icon sizes.

lessons.title: Common Controls
lessons.summary: The list view, tree view, status bar, progress bar and tab control come from the Common Controls library. This lesson enables visual styles, creates these controls, handles WM_NOTIFY, and uses a virtual list view to show a hundred thousand rows instantly.

projects.title: The model behind a virtual list

milestones.title: Drawing
milestones.blurb: Flicker-free drawing, Direct2D for fast antialiased graphics, DirectWrite for text, and images with WIC.

lessons.title: Flicker-Free Drawing
lessons.summary: Why windows flicker when they repaint, and the fixes - not erasing the background, drawing into an off-screen bitmap first, the buffered-paint API, painting only what changed, and scrolling content efficiently.

lessons.title: Drawing with Direct2D
lessons.summary: Direct2D draws antialiased shapes, gradients and bitmaps on the GPU. This lesson creates the factory and a render target for a window, separates device-independent and device-dependent resources, handles device loss, and uses transforms to move, rotate and scale drawings.

lessons.title: Text with DirectWrite
lessons.summary: DirectWrite lays out and renders text with proper font fallback, ligatures, colour emoji and ClearType. This lesson creates text formats and layouts, draws them with Direct2D, measures them, and uses hit-testing to place a caret and select text with the mouse.

lessons.title: Images with WIC
lessons.summary: The Windows Imaging Component decodes and encodes PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF and more. This lesson loads an image file, converts it to the pixel format Direct2D wants, draws it scaled with good quality, makes thumbnails, and explains premultiplied alpha.

milestones.title: The System
milestones.blurb: Files and directories, the registry and settings, processes, threads and synchronisation, and the clipboard, drag and drop and the shell.

lessons.title: Files and Directories
lessons.summary: Reading and writing files with CreateFileW, sharing modes and why "the file is in use", listing directories with FindFirstFileW, Windows paths and their traps (drive letters, UNC, long paths, reserved names), known folders, and watching a folder for changes.

lessons.title: The Registry and Settings
lessons.summary: The registry is Windows' hierarchical settings database. This lesson explains its structure, the per-user and per-machine hives, reading and writing values with RegGetValueW and RegSetValueExW, value types, and when a settings file in AppData is the better choice.

lessons.title: Processes
lessons.summary: Starting other programs from yours - CreateProcessW and its mutable command line, quoting arguments correctly, waiting for a child and reading its exit code, capturing its output through pipes, and opening documents with ShellExecuteExW.

lessons.title: Threads and Synchronisation
lessons.summary: Keeping the interface responsive while long work runs - worker threads, posting results back to the UI thread, protecting shared data with SRW locks and critical sections, events and condition variables, cancellation, and the thread pool.

lessons.title: Clipboard, Drag and Drop and the Shell
lessons.summary: Exchanging data with other programs - copying and pasting text through the clipboard, its formats and line endings, accepting files dropped from Explorer, file associations and the Recent list, and notifications in the taskbar.

milestones.title: Applications
milestones.blurb: A complete text editor, packaging and installing an application, and a file finder that searches on a worker thread.

lessons.title: Project: A Text Editor
lessons.summary: Build a complete Notepad-style editor - an edit control or your own text view, files opened and saved in their original encoding and line endings, undo, find and replace, a status bar with line and column, recent files, word wrap and fonts. This lesson is the plan, the key code, and the order to build it in.

tasks.title: Opening a file the way it was

lessons.title: Packaging and Installing
lessons.summary: Getting a Windows program onto other people's computers - the application manifest, version information, icons, static or dynamic runtime, per-user installs without administrator rights, MSIX and installers, code signing and SmartScreen, and updates.

lessons.title: Project: A File Finder
lessons.summary: Build a fast file search tool - a search box with options, a worker thread walking folders, results streaming into a virtual list view, sorting, progress and cancellation, opening results and showing them in Explorer. This lesson ties milestones 3 and 5 together.
